<script setup>
import { computed, reactive, ref } from "vue";

const saving = ref(false);
const form = reactive({ name: "", enabled: true, threshold: 10 });
const payload = computed(() => ({ ...form, threshold: Number(form.threshold) }));

async function save() {
  saving.value = true;
  try {
    await fetch("/api/config", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify(payload.value)
    });
  } finally {
    saving.value = false;
  }
}
</script>

import { ref, watch } from "vue";

const search = ref("");
const results = ref([]);

watch(search, async (term) => {
  if (!term) {
    results.value = [];
    return;
  }
  const response = await fetch(`/api/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(term)}`);
  results.value = await response.json();
});

groups.name: Recipes — SQL Schema Design & Query Foundations
groups.description: Contextual multi-step recipes retained because they demonstrate composition, lifecycle management or architecture. Prefer the direct API groups for individual symbols.

functions.name: users and roles schema with foreign key
functions.description: Baseline relational schema with timestamps and role relation.
functions.insertText:
CREATE TABLE roles (
  id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  label TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE users (
  id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
  role_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES roles(id),
  is_active BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
functions.longDescription: Good baseline for authentication-capable backends and admin tools.

functions.name: many to many join table
functions.description: Link two entities with a composite primary key.
functions.insertText:
CREATE TABLE project_members (
  project_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  user_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  role_code TEXT NOT NULL,
  added_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  PRIMARY KEY (project_id, user_id)
);
functions.longDescription: Use this when an entity can belong to many others without duplicating rows.

functions.name: soft delete columns and filtered query
functions.description: Track archival state without physically deleting rows.
functions.insertText:
ALTER TABLE documents
  ADD COLUMN deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  ADD COLUMN deleted_by BIGINT;

SELECT *
FROM documents
WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
ORDER BY created_at DESC;
functions.longDescription: A common requirement for business tools that need recovery and auditability.

functions.name: composite and partial index
functions.description: Index a filtered workload instead of the full table.
functions.longDescription: Useful for dashboards that query active rows far more often than archived data.

functions.name: check constraint for bounded status
functions.description: Constrain values at the database level.
functions.longDescription: Good complement to application validation because invalid states are rejected centrally.

functions.name: offset pagination query
functions.description: Simple page based pagination.
functions.insertText:
SELECT id, title, created_at
FROM articles
WHERE published_at IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT $1 OFFSET $2;
functions.longDescription: Easy to implement, though cursor pagination scales better for deep pages.

functions.name: cursor pagination query
functions.description: Stable pagination using a created_at/id cursor.
functions.insertText:
SELECT id, created_at, title
FROM articles
WHERE (created_at, id) < ($1, $2)
ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC
LIMIT $3;
functions.longDescription: Better fit than OFFSET when feeds or timelines grow large.

functions.name: upsert generic pattern
functions.description: Insert or update on conflict.
functions.insertText:
INSERT INTO feature_flags (key, enabled, updated_at)
VALUES ($1, $2, NOW())
ON CONFLICT (key)
DO UPDATE SET
  enabled = EXCLUDED.enabled,
  updated_at = NOW();
functions.longDescription: A standard pattern for settings tables and idempotent synchronization.

functions.name: optimistic locking with version column
functions.description: Prevent lost updates when multiple writers edit the same row.
functions.insertText:
UPDATE invoices
SET amount = $1,
    version = version + 1,
    updated_at = NOW()
WHERE id = $2
  AND version = $3;
functions.longDescription: Check affected row count in the backend to detect a concurrent modification.

functions.name: audit trigger updated_at concept
functions.description: Keep updated_at aligned with row changes.
functions.longDescription: A useful foundation when many tables share the same audit timestamp pattern.

functions.name: recursive tree query
functions.description: Read a hierarchy with a recursive CTE.
functions.insertText:
WITH RECURSIVE tree AS (
  SELECT id, parent_id, name, 0 AS depth
  FROM categories
  WHERE id = $1
  UNION ALL
  SELECT c.id, c.parent_id, c.name, t.depth + 1
  FROM categories c
  JOIN tree t ON c.parent_id = t.id
)
SELECT * FROM tree ORDER BY depth, name;
functions.longDescription: Useful for nested categories, trees, and menu structures.

functions.name: window function ranking
functions.description: Rank rows inside a group.
functions.insertText:
SELECT
  employee_id,
  department_id,
  salary,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC) AS salary_rank
FROM salaries;
functions.longDescription: Window functions are extremely useful for reporting endpoints and admin dashboards.
